questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: Pulse against tempo
questions.learningObjective: Identify pulses per minute from a tempo marking
questions.stem: A firmware engineer specifies a metronome tempo of 120 bpm; how many pulses occur in one minute?

options.text: one hundred twenty pulses, one per beat
sixty pulses, because bpm counts half-notes
options.misconception: halves the beat count by misreading bpm

options.text: two hundred forty pulses, doubling the count
options.misconception: doubles the beat count by confusing tempo with subdivisions

options.text: ninety pulses, applying an unsupported swing factor

questions.explanation: Bpm counts beats per minute, so 120 bpm yields 120 pulses. The distractors misread the unit or add unsupported factors.
questions.hint: One bpm equals one beat per minute.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: The beat unit in compound metre
questions.learningObjective: Identify the beat unit in compound meter
questions.stem: A brief for a 6/8 drum pattern asks which note value carries the beat in compound meter?

answer.exemplar: In compound meter the dotted quarter note carries the beat, grouping three eighth notes, so 6/8 has two dotted-quarter beats per measure.

questions.explanation: Compound meter groups in threes, so the dotted quarter note is the beat unit. Counting eighth notes as beats mistakes subdivision for beat.
questions.hint: Compound meter beats are dotted notes.

answer.exemplar: Three bars of 6/8 compound duple meter contain six dotted-quarter beats total, two per bar.

questions.explanation: Each 6/8 bar has two dotted-quarter beats, so three bars have six. Counting eighteen beats confuses subdivision.

questions.topic: The total duration of a measure
questions.stem: A design brief for a 5/4 track at 100 bpm asks how many seconds one measure lasts?
questions.explanation: At 100 bpm one beat lasts 0.6 seconds, and 5/4 has five beats, so one measure lasts three seconds.
